fine_trace.note: After consuming '<', the parser calls xmlParseQNameHashed to parse the element name from the input buffer.
The first character after '<' is a space (0x20), which fails the ASCII accelerator in xmlParseNCName, so control falls through to xmlParseNCNameComplex.
CUR_CHAR reads the current character; the space character is not a valid NCName start char, so the function returns with ret.name = NULL.
Since l.name is NULL and CUR is a space (not ':'), the function returns NULL without hashing.
The element name is NULL, so the parser reports an error and returns NULL. This path does not reach the vulnerable hash function.

The accelerator path in xmlParseNCName reads from the input buffer. When the name is at the end of the buffer and not null-terminated, xmlDictHashName reads one byte past the buffer end into adjacent global memory (xmlIsPubidChar_tab).

fine_trace.code: for (i = 0; i < maxLen && data[i]; i++) { HASH_UPDATE(h1, h2, data[i]); }
fine_trace.note: The loop reads data[i] until a null byte or maxLen. If the name buffer is not null-terminated within the input, the read at data[len] accesses one byte out-of-bounds before the global xmlIsPubidChar_tab table, causing the global-buffer-overflow READ.
